style: two parents taking turns on the log: dad is terse and lowercase and signs '-M'; mom is chatty with exclamation points and signs '-Jen'

situations.name: Parents going out to dinner with a sitter at home
situations.feared_outcome: You'll crash the car on the way home and I'll be stuck with the babysitter forever

behaviors.text: Calls mom's cell from the sitter's phone every 15-20 minutes to ask if they're on their way
Makes parents say the exact time they will be home and repeat it back before they leave

accommodations.text: Parents answer every call from home while they're out
Parents come home before Milo's bedtime so he doesn't fall asleep without them there

situations.name: Dad away on a work trip

behaviors.text: Won't lie down at bedtime until he has FaceTimed dad
Tracks dad's flight on the tablet and keeps asking mom if it has landed

accommodations.text: Dad sets a FaceTime at 8pm every night of the trip, stepping out of work dinners to do it
Mom lets Milo sleep in the parents' bed while dad is away

situations.name: Being on a different floor of the house from his parents

behaviors.text: Goes down to the basement playroom to build Legos, then runs back upstairs after a few minutes
Won't go upstairs alone to get something from his room

accommodations.text: A parent walks upstairs with him or stands at the bottom of the stairs talking to him

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: called jen's phone 5x from sitter's phone. 'are you coming yet'
monitoring_log.parent_response: jen picked up every time. we left before dessert. -M

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He took his Lego bin down to the basement all on his own!! Lasted maybe 4 minutes and then came FLYING up the stairs saying it was 'too quiet down there.'
monitoring_log.parent_response: I told him how brave it was to try and let him build at the kitchen table instead. -Jen

monitoring_log.situation: M flying to Denver for work
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Had the flight tracker up on the tablet basically all afternoon. Asked me 'did it land yet' probably ten times!  At dinner he asked what happens if a plane crashes.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I kept telling him it's still in the air, it's fine, and showed him the little plane on the map. -Jen

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: wouldn't get in bed until facetime
monitoring_log.parent_response: stepped out of client dinner at 8 to call. stayed on 15 min. -M

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He was okay after the FaceTime but asked to sleep in our bed again.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I said yes, it's only till Thursday!! Honestly I sleep better too. -Jen

monitoring_log.parent_words: needed his library book from his room. he would not go up alone. stood at the bottom of the stairs, made me come. I went up with him. -M

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Before we left he made us say what time we'd be home, three times, and repeat it back. 8:45. Then the calls started around 7.
monitoring_log.parent_response: We answered every call and we were home at 8:30 before he fell asleep, which was the deal. -Jen

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: wanted someone near. went up after i stood at stairs talking
monitoring_log.parent_response: stood at stairs, talked the whole time. -M
monitoring_log.trap: parent action written in child field

turns.text: Okay, everybody's here. Dad, you're on the laptop, can you hear us?
Yep. I can hear you.
Great. Milo, hi. Mom, hi. We have about ten minutes, so I'd like to go over the week, and then pick one thing to practice. Milo, I heard there was a big anniversary dinner.
They went to the fancy place. I had Kayla.
Kayla's the babysitter? How was it with Kayla?
Fine. But I called Mom a lot.
He did. I want to say five or six times. Starting around seven. And before we left he made us say what time we'd be home, and then he made us say it again, and then he said it back to us.
Milo, what were you checking for when you called?
If they were coming home yet.
And what's the worry? What's the scary thing that might happen if they're not coming home yet?
That they crash the car. And then I'm stuck with Kayla forever. Not forever forever. But like a really long time.

That's a big scary thought to have while you're eating pizza with Kayla. Thank you for telling me. Can you give it a number, the night they went to dinner? Zero is totally fine, ten is the most scared you've ever been.
Seven.
Seven. And when you called and Mom picked up, what happened to the seven?
It went down. And then it went up again.

That's such a good thing to notice. It goes down for a little while and then it climbs back up, and then you need to call again. That's how worries work. Calling feels good for a minute but it teaches the worry to keep asking. Dad, how about the trip? You were gone four nights, right?
Three. Monday to Thursday. Every night at eight I called. Stepped out of a client dinner one night. He wouldn't go to bed until we talked.
And he had the flight tracker up the whole afternoon when Marcus flew out. 'Did it land, did it land.' And he slept in our bed. I said yes every night, honestly.
Dad, from your side, if you had to put the trip on the thermometer for Milo, where would you put it?
Six. Lower than dinner out. He knows where I am on a trip.

Okay, six. That's an interesting difference. A trip is longer, but it's more predictable. A dinner out feels shorter, but in his head anything could happen on the drive. Those are two different worries even though both are about you leaving. Mom, the basement. You wrote that one up.
Yes! So he took his Legos down there by himself, which he never does. And then he came flying up after maybe four minutes. He said it was too quiet. So I let him build at the kitchen table.
Milo, I think going down there by yourself was really brave. What happened when it got too quiet?
I didn't know if anyone was still upstairs.
Ah. So you weren't sure people were still in the house. That's a lot like the dinner worry, isn't it? Wanting to check that everyone's where they should be.
Kind of.

Okay. Here's what I want to suggest for this week, and you all tell me if it's too much. Two things. First, the basement. Milo, how about you go down with the Lego bin and set a timer for five minutes. Mom or Dad stays upstairs. Nobody calls down, nobody comes down. When the timer goes off, you can come up and tell them what you built. Does five minutes sound doable?
Can I have music?
Hmm. Let's say no music for this one, because I want you to find out that the quiet is okay. If five minutes is too long, we can do three. What do you think?
Five. But only five.
Five it is. Every day if you can, at least three days. Second thing. Mom and Dad, is there another night out coming up?
My work thing on the twenty-fourth. Saturday.

Okay. For that night, here's the idea. Before you leave, you tell Milo one time when you'll be home. He doesn't repeat it back. And instead of answering every call, there's one planned call. Milo calls once at eight o'clock, Mom answers, and that's the only call. If he calls at other times, the phone doesn't get picked up, and you text Kayla to say you're fine.
Oh, that's going to be hard. For me, I mean.
I know. It's usually harder for the parents than the kid. Milo, what do you think about one call at eight?
What if it's an emergency?
Great question. If there's a real emergency, Kayla calls. Kayla knows what to do. You calling to check isn't an emergency, it's the worry asking. Deal?
Okay. Deal.
We'll do it.

Okay, recap. Basement with a five-minute timer, at least three days this week, nobody upstairs calls down. On the twenty-fourth, one time said once before you leave, and one planned call at eight. Keep writing in the log, both of you. And I'd like to hear about upstairs too, getting things from his room, next time. We didn't get to that today.
Sounds good. Thank you.
Bye!

topics: Anniversary dinner: Milo called mom 5-6 times from the sitter's phone and made parents repeat the return time
Milo's feared outcome: parents crash the car and he is stuck with the sitter
Dad's three-night work trip: nightly 8pm FaceTime, flight tracking, Milo slept in parents' bed
Basement: Milo went down alone and came back up after about four minutes because it was too quiet
Getting things from upstairs alone was not discussed and is for next time
agreed: Milo plays in the basement alone with a five-minute timer, no music, at least three days this week; parents stay upstairs and do not call down
On the next night out (Saturday the 24th) parents say the return time once, Milo does not repeat it back, and there is one planned call at 8pm; other calls are not answered
Both parents keep writing the log

must_not_appear: Dad agreed to cancel or shorten his next work trip
A Fear Level for the basement or for going upstairs
Milo is allowed music in the basement
Mom agreed to stop letting Milo sleep in the parents' bed
